buttermilk
No buttermilk: 1 cup milk + 1 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar, rested 5 min.
crème fraîche
Sub: sour cream (finish off-heat; it splits where crème fraîche holds) or Greek yogurt loosened with cream.
galangal
Ginger stands in, with the honest warning it becomes a different, softer soup.
lemongrass
Sub: strips of lime zest + a little lime juice; the perfume narrows but survives.
makrut
Sub: bay leaf + generous lime zest, added late.
fish sauce
Sub: soy sauce + pinch of salt; vegetarians: soy + a little miso for the missing depth.
shaoxing
Sub: dry sherry (closest) or mirin minus a pinch of the recipe’s sugar.
mirin
Sub: 1 tbsp sake or dry sherry + 1 tsp sugar per tbsp mirin.
sake
Sub: dry sherry or dry white wine.
gochujang
Sub: miso + chili flakes + a touch of honey — the ferment is approximate, the direction right.
tamarind
Sub: lime juice + a little brown sugar; less fruity, same sour spine.
palm sugar
Sub: light brown sugar, slightly less.
guanciale
Sub: pancetta (closest) or thick bacon, blanched 1 min to mute the smoke.
pancetta
Sub: thick-cut bacon, blanched briefly to soften the smoke, or guanciale if you’re lucky.
mascarpone
Sub: cream cheese beaten with a splash of heavy cream.
pecorino
Sub: Parmigiano + a pinch more salt, gentler, but the dish survives.
gruyère
Sub: comté, emmental, or a young alpine-style; low-moisture mozzarella melts right but tastes shy.
shallot
Sub: the sweet half of a small onion + a whisper of garlic.
chipotle
Sub: smoked paprika + cayenne, smoke and heat reassembled.
guajillo
Sub: ancho (sweeter) or New Mexico chiles; paprika + cayenne in exile.
ancho
Sub: guajillo or mulato; or 1 tbsp paprika + pinch cocoa per chile.
sumac
Sub: lemon zest + a small squeeze of juice, added off-heat.
za'atar
Sub: dried thyme + toasted sesame + sumac (or lemon zest) + salt.
harissa
Sub: sriracha + smoked paprika + ground caraway.
white miso
Sub: yellow miso (stronger: use less) or a mashed splash of soy + tahini.
tahini
Sub: smooth natural peanut butter or sunflower-seed butter, nuttier, still right.
pomegranate molasses
Sub: reduce pomegranate juice with sugar and lemon to a syrup.
curry leaves
No true sub: a bay leaf + lime zest gestures at it; better to omit than fake.
masa harina
Sub: nothing replaces nixtamal for tortillas; for thickening, fine cornmeal at half quantity.
semolina
Sub: fine cornmeal (for dusting) or all-purpose flour (in dough, texture softens).
bread flour
Sub: all-purpose + 1 tsp vital wheat gluten per cup; or accept a slightly softer crumb.
cake flour
Sub (per cup): all-purpose minus 2 tbsp, plus 2 tbsp cornstarch, sifted twice.
heavy cream
Sub (cooking, not whipping): ¾ cup milk + ¼ cup melted butter.
gelatin
Vegetarian: agar-agar, use about half, and know it sets firmer and hotter.
dry sherry
Sub: dry vermouth or dry white wine.
oyster sauce
Sub: hoisin thinned with soy (sweeter), or vegetarian mushroom oyster sauce.
black vinegar
Sub: balsamic + a splash of rice vinegar.
rice vinegar
Sub: apple cider vinegar diluted with a little water.
cotija
Sub: feta (closest crumble) or ricotta salata.
queso fresco
Sub: mild feta rinsed of brine, or paneer crumbled.
paneer
Sub: halloumi (saltier: rinse) or extra-firm tofu, pressed.
plantain
Green: sub yuca or potato for texture, not flavor. Ripe: sub nothing — wait for the plantain.
tomatillo
Sub: green tomatoes + a squeeze of lime.
lard
Sub: butter (flavor) or shortening (texture); duck fat where luxury permits.
ghee
Sub: clarified butter (same thing, younger) or butter + a spoon of neutral oil.
saffron
No true sub: turmeric fakes the color only; use less of the dish’s pride and more of its patience.
star anise
Sub: ½ tsp five-spice per pod, or fennel seed + a clove.
fresh yeast
Sub: instant yeast at one-third the weight.
crema
Sub: sour cream loosened with a little lime juice and milk.
dashi
Sub: light chicken stock + splash of soy; vegetarian: kombu-shiitake steep.
